sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 3.1 'The sound system' (pp. 8-9) gives a consonant chart (p, t, ch, k, b, d, j, q, v, s, gh, m, n, ng, l, r), a five-vowel chart and English-comparison pronunciation notes; sec. 3.2 covers alphabet problems. No mention of stress, accent, vowel length or prosody anywhere in the 50-page scan (a full-text search for stress/accent the scanned layer). Describes the Ghaimuta dialect (Glottolog ghai1237) from one week's fieldwork in Lame village, Nov. 1977.
Nothing on stress; reports 6 vowels (Unger 2008: 5) and 15 consonants with prenasalized voiced stops (Unger 2008: 4), plus pronoun and verb-phrase material; second-hand and silent on accent.

sources.citation: Unger, Paul. 2019. Reduced Reduplication in Doku [lgr]: Geminate Consonants and Stressed Vowel Syncope in Southeast Solomonic. In Brenda H. Boerger and Paul Unger (eds.), Selected Proceedings from the Tenth Conference on Oceanic Linguistics (COOL10), 24-38. SIL Language and Culture Documentation and Description 45. Dallas: SIL International (paper also issued separately as SIL LCDD 43).

tone.quote: As might be expected, “reduced” syllables affect stress patterns. Reduced reduplication necessitates a couple of stress realignments since stress in Doku is generally on penultimate syllables.14 First, when reduplication happens, stress is assigned following the general pattern; that is, it remains on—or moves to, in the case of single syllable stems—the penultimate syllable as required. ... [fn. 14:] This is not “hard and fast.” Trisyllabic exceptions include: /ˈᵐbo.ᵐbo.lo/ ‘pomelo’, /ˈgi.li.o/ ‘dolphin’, /ˈsa.li.u/ ‘overshoot’, /ˈsi.ᵑɡi.o/ ‘snail’, /ˈsi.mi.u/ ‘parcelling leaf’, /ˈsi.pi.u/ ‘octopus’, and /ˈva.nu.a/ ‘village’.
tone.locator: p. 31 with footnote 14, section 3 'Reduced reduplication' of the 179-p. LCDD 45 volume (paper = printed 24-38)
